# PLAN — iteration 3
## Current state assessment
The incumbent is already timing-feasible at 3 LUTs and 4 FFs, so this iteration must strictly reduce LUTs without increasing them and must still pass every verification and metric gate. Iteration 1’s equivalent inline binary counter matched the incumbent’s resource use; iteration 2’s 4-bit Johnson counter increased both LUTs and FFs.

## Hypothesis
A 3-bit down-counter that reloads to 7 when `noisy` matches `clean` and counts down on mismatches may let Vivado share the decrement borrow logic with terminal detection, reducing LUT use while retaining the same four state bits and cycle behavior.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the child instance with equivalent logic inside `debouncer_top`, keeping `// @latency 0`, a registered `clean` output, and a 3-bit counter. Reset the counter to 7; clear it back to 7 when `noisy == clean`, otherwise decrement it and update `clean` to `noisy` when the pre-decrement count is zero, then reload to 7. Preserve synchronous active-high reset priority and the exact eighth-consecutive-mismatch update; do not use the previously tried binary up-counter or 4-bit Johnson encoding.
